amber.note: Ground of the front half of the sheet, and the flipped type colour inside an inverted element on that ground. Never a fill.

ink.note: All primary text on both grounds, every solid fill, the plate border, the selection highlight and the scrollbar thumb.

oxblood.note: The contact ink: hover, the copied state, inline code in the docs, and the second speaker. Type and rules only, never a fill.

paper.note: Ground of the reverse half of the sheet (.invert), and the flipped type colour inside an inverted element on that ground.

ink-quiet-on-amber.note: Secondary and supporting text on the amber ground. Re-declared rather than reused across grounds.

ink-quiet-on-paper.note: Secondary and supporting text on the paper ground, set by .invert.

rule.note: The hairline between blocks: band edges, section tops, column divisions. Re-declared at 0.24 under .invert.

rule-faint.note: The hairline inside a block: fact rows, key/value rows, docs links. Re-declared at 0.11 under .invert.

display.purpose: The two poster headlines. Flush-set to the measure by measurement, not by the clamp; the clamp is the fallback.

billing-1.purpose: Top-billed act heading. Highest rank on the sheet below the display line.

billing-3.purpose: Third-rank act heading; also the models and privacy acts on the reverse of the sheet.

billing-4.purpose: Lowest act rank; the closing factual act.

title.purpose: Sub-headings inside an act: point runs, requirement blocks, model names, docs sections.

lead.purpose: The one-line sub under a headline and the prose column of an act. Capped at 62ch.

caption.purpose: Plate captions, command lines, secondary notes.

label.purpose: The smallest voice: the marginalia run, the footer, plate identifiers, docs group headings. Always uppercase.

mono.purpose: Only where there is a real command, file size, spec value or timecode. Never atmosphere.

motion.name: contact
motion.purpose: Colour and rule-colour change on hover of a ruled action. Colour only; nothing moves.

motion.name: inversion
motion.purpose: Background and text swap when an element inverts out of the sheet.

motion.name: billing-step
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: font-size and font-variation-settings stepping as an act takes or gives up top billing in the bill. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, where rank survives as the inversion and the struck rule.

motion.name: chip-state
motion.purpose: Active-state colour change on the overlay stage's progress chips.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter narrows to 22px; every two-column grid collapses to one; point runs swap left hairlines for top hairlines; docs sidebar unsticks.

breakpoints.name: hand
breakpoints.purpose: The bill of acts and the language pair leave the top line and fold into a toggled panel; command lines wrap; key/value rows stack.

screens.name: turn-of-sheet
screens.purpose: The mechanical halftone band that marks where the sheet turns from amber to paper. The only mid-tone device in the system.

screens.name: speaker-band
screens.value: radial-gradient(circle at center, currentColor 0 1.15px, transparent 1.15px) 0 100% / 5px 5px repeat-x
screens.purpose: A screen of one speaker's own ink, printed as a band along the baseline rather than behind the glyph, so the word keeps its silhouette.

measure.name: sheet
measure.purpose: The one measure. Everything but band grounds and the screened band lives inside it.

measure.name: gutter
measure.purpose: Sheet gutter, narrowing at the 1080px breakpoint.

measure.name: reading
measure.purpose: Cap on lead and prose columns (.measure).

measure.name: tail
measure.purpose: The justified tail block at the foot of the sheet.

foreignScopes.note: Untouched reproductions of the macOS app's own UI: its .light cream palette, Space Grotesk and Hanken Grotesk faces, 14px rounded window and shadows. Deliberately a foreign world printed onto the sheet. Not part of this design system; its tokens are never a source for a page decision, and page tokens are never pushed into it. The sheet's only intervention is the .win reset that mounts a mock as a flat plate.

narrative.overview:
The site is one sheet of paper, printed both sides. The front is drenched amber edge to edge; the back -- the dense factual half where the models, the privacy claims and the requirements live -- is the same sheet turned over to paper cream. A mechanical dot screen marks the turn. Nothing on the page is a card, a panel, a tile or a container. Sections are bands of the same sheet divided by a hairline, and hierarchy is carried by size and line breaks alone, the way a concert bill ranks its acts: the headliner is simply the largest type on the poster, and no numeral, kicker or eyebrow is ever printed to explain the order.

The world is deliberately the opposite of what this software category ships. It refuses the centred hero over a radial glow, the alternating zig-zag feature rows, the trio of icon-tile cards and the gradient CTA box. In their place: a headline flush-set to the full measure by measurement rather than by a clamp, acts that descend in billing size down the page, a justified tail block packing the smallest facts at the foot, and a marginalia run across the very top that is the sheet's own first line rather than a floating bar -- it scrolls away with the paper.

The only picture on the page is the software actually running. Every image is live HTML and CSS: five reproductions of the real macOS app, mounted as plates with a hard ink edge. That is the whole proof strategy, and it is why the sheet carries no photography, no illustration, no decorative shape and no social proof of any kind.
keyCharacteristics: Four inks, closed set; every intermediate tone is a halftone screen, never a blend
One variable grotesk at eight steps, condensing as it grows
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero glass on the page's own chrome
Rules are hairlines; state is inversion
Nothing enters, fades or slides; the one authored motion changes rank, not visibility

rules.name: The Four Inks Rule
rules.body: Amber, ink, oxblood, paper. There is no fifth colour and no gradient anywhere in the page's own chrome. If a tone between two inks is needed, it is printed as a mechanical dot screen -- a repeating radial-gradient dot on a 9px grid for the band that marks the turn of the sheet, and a 5px dot band along the baseline behind each speaker's name. A screen is a pattern of one ink; it is never a blend of two.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The active, current or featured state is one move: fill with ink, flip the type to the ground colour. This is the entire state vocabulary of the page. It is used for the act in play in the bill, the default model row, the active docs-sidebar link, the current language, and text selection. Nothing glows, tints, outlines or lifts to say "selected".

rules.name: The Contact-Only Oxblood Rule
rules.body: Oxblood is earned by touch or by identity -- hover, the copied confirmation, the other speaker -- and by nothing else. The moment oxblood becomes a fill or a resting decoration, the four-ink system reads as a three-plus-accent system and the poster becomes a website.

rules.name: The Flush-Set Rule
rules.body: The two display headlines are not sized by a clamp. A typesetter in site.js measures each line at a 100px reference, scales it so it fills the container's width exactly, then runs one correction pass. The block squares off instead of ragging wherever a clamp happened to stop. The CSS clamp is the fallback that shows before the measurement runs and stands if it never does -- it is not the design. The fit re-runs on resize and again on document.fonts.ready.

rules.name: The Authored Break Rule
rules.body: Headline lines are authored per locale in _data/*.json as hero.titleLines, rebroken to comparable lengths so that flush-setting cannot leave one line towering over its neighbour. French runs longer than English and gets its own breaks. A headline is never handed to the browser to wrap.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Archivo does every job. JetBrains Mono appears only where there is a real command, size or timecode. A third face on the page's own surfaces is a system violation.

rules.name: The Rank-By-Size Rule
rules.body: Acts are not peers, and size is the only thing carrying the difference. Each act heading takes a permanent billing tier (.bill-1 ... .bill-4) that descends down the sheet, with plateaus where two acts share a rank. Rank is never printed as a numeral, a kicker, an eyebrow, a step label or a coloured tag.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: A section is a band of the sheet, separated from its neighbour by one hairline. Nothing on this page is a card. If a block needs to be set apart, it is set apart by a rule, a column division or an inversion -- not by a box with a background, a border radius and an inset.

rules.name: The Sheet's Own First Line Rule
rules.body: The marginalia run at the top is not a floating bar. It has no fixed position, no backdrop blur, no shadow and no compact scrolled state; it is the top line of the sheet and it scrolls away with the paper.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on any element the page owns. If a surface needs to be distinguished, use a hairline, an inversion, or a screened band. Shadows belong to the app being pictured, not to the sheet it is printed on.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: A screen of the app mounts as a plate: border-radius 0, box-shadow none, outline none, and a 1px ink border -- all forced with !important over the mock's own window chrome. A poster does not float a window, it prints a plate.

dos: Do build every new surface out of bands divided by hairlines, inside the 1360px measure with the 40px/22px gutter.
Do carry rank with billing size and authored line breaks. If a new section needs to outrank its neighbour, give it a higher .bill- tier.
Do use inversion -- ink fill, ground-coloured type -- as the only way to say active, current, featured or selected.
Do reserve the width of an element's largest state whenever state changes its type size, so no row reflows.
Do reach for a mechanical dot screen when a mid-tone is genuinely needed, at the established scales (1.6px on 9px, 1.15px on 5px).
Do re-declare --fg-2, --rule and --rule-faint for any new ground, the way .invert does, instead of letting one value carry across both sheets.
Do re-run any measurement-based layout on document.fonts.ready; a width measured against the fallback face is the wrong width.
Do keep every text role at or above the 5.26:1 floor this build measured against its own ground.
Do set commands, file sizes, spec values and timecodes in JetBrains Mono, and nothing else.
donts: Don't introduce a fifth colour, a gradient, a tint or an opacity-blended tone on the page's own chrome. The one gradient on the page lives inside the pinned brand logo.
Don't add a border radius, a shadow, a blur, a glass surface or a translucent layer. There is no elevation in this system.
Don't build a card, a panel, a tile, a bordered box around body text or a trio of icon tiles. A filled panel never sits behind body text.
Don't make a button a pill or a filled rounded block. Actions are type over a rule.
Don't float the top run, shrink it on scroll, or give it a backdrop blur.

Don't animate anything into existence. No @keyframes, no animation, no transform, no entrance, no scroll reveal, no parallax. Content is fully visible at all times, and the only authored motion changes rank.
Don't print rank as a numeral, a kicker, an eyebrow, a step label or a coloured tag.
Don't fill an area with oxblood or put it behind text; it is a contact and identity ink for type and rules.
Don't add photography, illustration, decorative shapes, or any social proof -- logos, counts, testimonials, stars. The app mocks are the only demonstration this site makes.
Don't let a headline wrap on its own. Author the breaks per locale.
Don't fold the mock palette or the mock faces into the page's system.

divergences.contract: The headline sets in three lines.
divergences.built: Two flush-set lines per locale, authored in _data/en.json and _data/fr.json as hero.titleLines.
divergences.reason: Three flush lines filled the measure but pushed the live-meeting plate out of the first viewport, and both were contract promises. Two lines keep both. The finish reviewer endorsed the two-line setting and asked that it be recorded here.

divergences.contract: The billing size-step plays on the act headings: the act in play steps up a size and its neighbours demote.
divergences.built: The act headings keep permanent billing tiers (.bill-1 ... .bill-4). The step, the demotion and the struck-off state play in the bill -- the marginalia run across the top -- with each name reserving the width of its largest state so the row never shifts.
divergences.reason: The act headings are full sentences that sit on a wrap boundary at almost any measure. Stepping their size either gained a line, which made the emphasised setting read worse than the quiet one, or, once capped to preserve the line count, produced no visible step at all. The intent is unchanged -- the act in play takes top billing -- only where it is printed.

provenance.rasters: This build produced no shipping rasters. Every image on the page is live HTML and CSS (the app mocks). The PNGs in site/src/ -- og-en.png, og-fr.png, apple-touch-icon.png, icon-192.png, icon-512.png -- are pre-existing social-preview and favicon assets committed before this build and never render on the page. The remaining PNGs in the repo are review screenshots under .impeccable/review/, which is gitignored.
provenance.typography: Archivo variable (weight 100-900, width 62%-125%) and JetBrains Mono variable, both self-hosted as woff2 under site/src/fonts/.
measured: Four inks only: amber #e2a22f ground, ink #17100a, oxblood #6b2710, paper #fbf3e2.
Every sampled text role measures at least 5.26:1 against its own ground.
Detector clean, exit 0, with one inline waiver in site.css for the .mock-scoped Space Grotesk face.
No @keyframes, no animation, no transform, no box-shadow outside the .win reset, no non-zero border-radius on the page's own chrome, and no entrance motion anywhere.
